pageProps.title: A Night of Murder Without a Perpetrator
pageProps.review: Keigo Higashino's early short story collection A Night of Murder Without a Perpetrator sharply explores the nature hidden within us and the banality of evil through the tragic butterfly effect brought about by the minor malice and intent of ordinary people.
pageProps.content:
## Review An early short story collection by the author, it has one strong theme: how minor malice leads to catastrophic results. It explores the ```banality of evil``` residing within ordinary people we commonly see around us, rather than a giant conspiracy or a psychopathic villain.
A very small intent is tracked as it amplifies like a butterfly effect and leads to an irreversible tragedy. It shows that even a seemingly ordinary and good human can harbor seeds of cruel destruction within.
As it is an early work of the author, some ```clumsiness``` in unrealistic setups or rough development can be felt.
